fields.spec_version: TI TFP410 datasheet revision D (February 2024) — implements DVI 1.0 + HDMI video-only.
previous_versions: TFP410 Rev B / C — incremental documentation updates.
TFP410 Rev D (February 2024) — current revision; production data; modernized format.
DVI 1.0 (April 1999) — Digital Display Working Group (DDWG) specification; the protocol TFP410 implements. Defines TMDS encoding, pixel rate up to 165 MHz, single-link / dual-link configurations.
HDMI 1.0 (December 2002) — backward-compatible with DVI 1.0 video; adds audio data-island, AVI / Audio InfoFrame packets, HDCP, CEC bus. TFP410 is video-only — does NOT emit HDMI audio islands.
HDMI 1.1 (May 2004) — adds DVD-Audio support; not relevant to TFP410.
HDMI 1.2 (August 2005) — adds support for One Bit Audio; not relevant.
HDMI 1.3 (June 2006) — raises pixel clock to 340 MHz (single-link); adds Deep Color (≥ 10 bit/component) + xvYCC; TFP410 does NOT support 340 MHz or Deep Color.
HDMI 1.4 (June 2009) — adds 4K@30Hz, HDMI Ethernet Channel (HEC), Audio Return Channel (ARC), 3D formats. TFP410 does NOT support these.
HDMI 2.0 (September 2013) — pixel clock to 600 MHz; 4K@60Hz; not supported by TFP410.
HDMI 2.1 (November 2017) — Fixed Rate Link (FRL); 8K@60Hz; eARC; not supported by TFP410.

key_changes.summary: HDMI adds backward-compatible video preamble + guard band before pixel data, audio data-island in vertical blanking (TERC4-encoded), Type-A connector, AVI / Audio / SPD / MPEG / Source / Vendor InfoFrames, HDCP authentication. TFP410 is HDMI-video-only — it emits DVI-compatible TMDS without HDMI preamble / data island / InfoFrames.
Pixel clock 165 → 340 MHz; Deep Color 10/12/16-bit per component; xvYCC color space. TFP410 max pixel clock remains 165 MHz.
3D formats (frame-packed / side-by-side / top-and-bottom); HEC (Ethernet); ARC (audio return); 4K@30Hz. TFP410 does NOT support.
Pixel clock 340 → 600 MHz; 4K@60Hz; YUV 4:2:0 to keep bandwidth. TFP410 max 165 MHz.
FRL replaces TMDS for 8K and high-rate modes; eARC. Wire-level encoding is no longer TMDS in FRL mode. TFP410 is TMDS-only.
Documentation modernization; production-data status; clarified I2C register descriptions; no silicon change.

backward_compat_traps.rule: TFP410 emits DVI 1.0-compliant TMDS — i.e. pure video + control characters + sync. It does NOT emit HDMI video preamble, guard band, audio data island, or InfoFrames.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Connecting TFP410 to an HDMI-strict sink that requires preamble + guard band to enable display may result in receiver waiting for valid HDMI framing and not displaying anything. Most HDMI receivers fall back to DVI-compatible mode when preamble is absent.

backward_compat_traps.rule: CTL[3] is reserved for HDCP and TFP410 always encodes it as 0. CTL[2:1] are user-controllable.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Software that drives CTL[3] expecting it to appear on TX2 will see no effect. HDCP cipher itself is NOT inside TFP410 — system-level HDCP must drive a separate authentication block.
Driving > 165 MHz pushes the PLL outside its lock range; TMDS output may go undefined; no error reported in TFP410.

backward_compat_traps.rule: After RESET, CTL_1_MODE.PD = 0 (powered down). Device does NOT auto-enable TMDS until host writes PD=1 over I2C.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Software that assumes TFP410 wakes up to normal operation after reset will see no TMDS output until PD is set.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Differential IDCK input is only available when V_REF ≤ 0.9 V (low-swing mode).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Attempting differential clock in high-swing mode (V_REF=DV_DD) silently falls back to single-ended sensing.

backward_compat_traps.rule: When ISEL=0, BSEL/DSEL/EDGE pins drive the input configuration. When ISEL=1, I2C register CTL_1_MODE bits (BSEL/DSEL/EDGE) override the pin straps.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Mismatched pin straps and register writes can lead to confusing config-change behaviour.

backward_compat_traps.rule: TFP410 base I2C address = 0b0111_A3A2A1; A[3:1] are pin-strapped to CTL3/CTL2/CTL1 pins (pins 6/7/8). The 7-bit address therefore depends on hardware straps.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Software with hardcoded 0x70 base will fail to address a TFP410 whose A[3:1] straps are non-zero. Use register-discovery (read VEN_ID = 0x014C) to confirm.

backward_compat_traps.rule: I2C 7-bit DDC EDID device address is 0x50; on the wire including the R/W bit the byte is 0xA0 (write) / 0xA1 (read).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Confusing 7-bit and 8-bit address representation is a common DDC bug; use 0x50 in I2C controller library that takes 7-bit, or 0xA0 in libraries that take 8-bit + R/W.

backward_compat_traps.rule: TFP410 does NOT generate HDMI audio data islands or InfoFrames. Audio over HDMI requires a separate HDMI audio packetizer.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Building an HDMI source from TFP410 alone yields a video-only HDMI signal; receivers will not produce audio.

backward_compat_traps.rule: TFP410 TMDS pairs are DC-coupled to the receiver's 50 Ω termination to AV_DD.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Adding AC coupling capacitors on the TMDS pairs breaks RSEN sense and may break the receiver's bias point — DO NOT AC-couple DVI/HDMI 1.x TMDS lines.

fields.version_naming_history_note: TFP410 has shipped continuously since October 2001 across SLDS145 revisions A→D with no silicon revision; SLDS145D (February 2024) is the latest datasheet revision. DVI 1.0 (1999) and HDMI 1.0 video-only (2002) are the relevant protocol specifications. TFP410 does NOT support HDMI 1.3+ Deep Color, HDMI 1.4+ 3D / HEC / ARC, HDMI 2.x high-rate FRL, or any HDCP version (cipher outside chip). For modern HDMI 2.x / 2.1 designs use a current HDMI transmitter such as TI TMDS181, TMDS261, or similar.
